chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Take a donkey to carry your belongings, for its sustenance is upon God.'

He said: So I acquired a donkey, and I and my brother Yusuf — when a year was completed — would calculate our expenditures to know their amount. So we calculated our expenditures after purchasing the donkey, and they were the same as they had always been every year — nothing had increased.

key_terms.رَحْل: Belongings, luggage, or travel gear — one's worldly possessions and necessities
key_terms.رِزْق: Divinely ordained provision and sustenance — what God has allocated for a creature's needs
key_terms.نَفَقَات: Expenditures, ongoing expenses — what is spent for livelihood and upkeep

ai.seo_question: Does Islam teach that God provides for animals if we care for them?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised his companion Yunus ibn Ya'qub to acquire a donkey for travel, assuring him that God would provide for it without burdening his own finances. The narrator confirms this through a practical test: after buying the donkey and tracking yearly expenses carefully, he and his brother Yusuf found that their total expenditures remained unchanged. This hadith illustrates the Shia teaching of tawakkul (reliance on God) in practical matters — that those who trust in God's provision will find it sufficient.
